meta.subtitle: From the February 2022 spin-off out of Exelon Corporation through the September 2024 Three Mile Island Microsoft 20-year PPA into the structural repricing of US merchant nuclear baseload
meta.abstract: Constellation Energy Corporation (CEG, NASDAQ) is the Baltimore-headquartered owner and operator of the largest US nuclear power generation fleet — 22 reactors at 14 sites with approximately 32 gigawatts of zero-emissions capacity, plus an additional 6+ gigawatts of natural gas, hydroelectric, wind, and solar generation. The company emerged from Exelon Corporation through the February 1, 2022 corporate separation that established the regulated utility business (continuing as Exelon Corporation) and the merchant generation business (becoming Constellation Energy). Joseph Dominguez became CEO of the post-spin Constellation entity, having led Exelon's Pennsylvania utilities through the pre-spin period; CFO Daniel Eggers joined December 2021 just before the spin completion. The single most consequential commercial event in the post-spin history was the September 20, 2024 announcement of a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 (now branded the Crane Clean Energy Center after the former Exelon CEO Christopher Crane) for approximately 835 megawatts of nuclear baseload supply to Microsoft data centre operations. The transaction priced Microsoft-grade carbon-free baseload at levels well above traditional merchant nuclear baseload pricing and established the template for subsequent hyperscaler-utility nuclear PPA structures. Fiscal year 2025 (calendar year 2025) produced adjusted EBITDA in the approximate $4.5-5.5 billion range and adjusted operating earnings in the high single digits per share range. The board is chaired by Mayo Shattuck III (the former Constellation Energy Group Chairman/CEO/President who led the original Constellation through its 2012 merger with Exelon and chairs the post-2022-spin Constellation Energy through the new era), and includes a slate of directors with deep utility, finance, and broader industry experience. The investment proposition compresses AI data centre electricity demand sustainability, the structural pricing power of carbon-free baseload nuclear in a tightening grid, the operating economics of an aging US nuclear fleet with relicensing extensions to the 2050s and 2060s, and the potential for additional restart transactions (Palisades Michigan restart by Holtec is a parallel industry event; Three Mile Island Unit 1 is the Constellation-specific restart).

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
On September 20, 2024, Constellation Energy Corporation set a marker for the US merchant-power sector. The company announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft for the restarted Three Mile Island Unit 1, renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center, a structure Constellation later described as selling Microsoft the plant's energy, capacity, and emissions-free attributes once the unit returned to service. The public significance was less a disclosed price than a disclosed commitment: a hyperscale customer had agreed to anchor the restart of a shuttered nuclear asset with a 20-year bilateral contract at full-facility scale. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Company Profile

Constellation Energy Corporation (CEG, NASDAQ) was headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland. By the frozen snapshot date, the company said it had ownership interests in 14 nuclear generating stations currently in service, consisting of 25 units and approximately 22 gigawatts of nuclear capacity, which produced 183 terawatt-hours of zero-emissions electricity in 2025. The operating fleet spanned PJM, MISO, NYISO, and ERCOT through the South Texas Project, while the Crane Clean Energy Center remained a restart project rather than an operating station. Around that nuclear core sat a smaller portfolio of gas, hydro, wind, and solar generation, plus a competitive retail and wholesale supply business that extended across deregulated markets including ISO-NE. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

The company was formed through the February 1, 2022 spin-off from Exelon Corporation, which retained the regulated utility subsidiaries ComEd, PECO, BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, and ACE. Joseph Dominguez was chief executive of the newly independent company. Daniel Eggers, who had joined as chief financial officer in December 2021, carried the finance function through the separation; after the Calpine close in January 2026, Eggers moved to the role of Senior Executive Vice President, Finance and Data Economy, Shane Smith became chief financial officer, and Robert J. Lawless served as non-executive chair. [Constellation leadership changes](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-announces-key-senior-leadership-changes-ahead/); [Constellation 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000140/e26004_ceg-def14a.htm)

## Financial Baseline

The post-spin earnings story was not a simple top-line march higher. Official results showed operating revenues of $24.442 billion in 2022, $24.918 billion in 2023, $23.568 billion in 2024, and $25.533 billion in 2025. In that same sequence, adjusted EBITDA rose from $2.667 billion in 2022 to $4.025 billion in 2023, while later company disclosures emphasised adjusted operating earnings per share of $8.67 in 2024 and $9.39 in 2025. The pattern reflected an earnings mix transformed by Section 45U, higher capacity prices, and later the expanding data-centre and Calpine platform story, rather than a clean linear progression in revenue alone. [Constellation FY2022 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2022-results); [Constellation FY2023 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2023-results); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

| Fiscal Year | Operating revenue | Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted operating EPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | $24.442bn | $2.667bn | - |
| FY2023 | $24.918bn | $4.025bn | - |
| FY2024 | $23.568bn | - | $8.67 |
| FY2025 | $25.533bn | - | $9.39 |

## The IRA Floor

The Inflation Reduction Act's Section 45U production tax credit was the structural element that remade the investment case. Constellation's 10-K described the credit as applying to existing nuclear generation from 2024 through 2032, at up to $15 per megawatt-hour subject to phase-out mechanics tied to realised power prices and compliance with wage and apprenticeship requirements. In practice, the credit turned part of merchant nuclear's historical downside into a policy floor, while PJM's 2025-2026 base residual auction cleared at $269.92 per megawatt-day and established a second source of earnings support. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [PJM 2025-2026 BRA release](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2024-releases/20240730-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-sufficient-resources-to-meet-rto-reliability-requirement.pdf)

## A Second Hyperscaler

The Microsoft contract at Crane established the commercial template; the second proof point arrived on June 3, 2025, when Constellation announced a 20-year agreement with Meta for the full output of the Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois. Constellation said the arrangement began in June 2027, supported the plant's continued operation into mid-century, and included a 30-megawatt uprate expected to be fully complete in 2029. The company also said the agreement would preserve 1,100 local jobs, sustain roughly $13.5 million of annual tax revenue, and include $1 million of charitable giving over five years. [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## The Calpine Acquisition

While the hyperscaler PPA strategy was taking shape, Constellation also moved to transform its generation platform in size and fuel mix. On January 10, 2025, the company announced an agreement to acquire Calpine. Constellation described the transaction as an equity purchase price of about $16.4 billion, made up of 50 million newly issued CEG shares and $4.5 billion of cash, together with the assumption of about $12.7 billion of Calpine net debt; after expected cash generation and tax attributes, the announced enterprise value was about $26.6 billion. The transaction closed on January 7, 2026, and Constellation said the combined company then had approximately 55 gigawatts of generating capacity and about 2.5 million customer accounts. [Constellation - Calpine announcement](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-acquire-calpine-creates-americas-leading-producer); [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

## The Central Question

By the frozen week, CEG's valuation had become enormous. Constellation's own historic price lookup showed a May 22, 2026 closing price of $294.07, and the proxy stated that 313,309,685 common shares were outstanding as of March 2, 2026. On that basis, the equity market value stood at roughly $92.1 billion near the frozen snapshot date. [Constellation historic price lookup](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/stock-information/historic-price-lookup); [Constellation 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000140/e26004_ceg-def14a.htm)

From that base, the central analytical questions were threefold. First, could the hyperscaler template established at Crane and extended at Clinton be replicated across more of the uncontracted nuclear fleet? Second, would Calpine's gas and geothermal assets widen Constellation's margin and customer reach without diluting the nuclear premium? Third, how durable would the AI-driven electricity demand cycle prove once PJM capacity prices, NRC timing, and the post-2032 tax-policy horizon were tested in practice? As of May 23, 2026, Constellation's official disclosures pointed to a 2027 return-to-service target for Crane. [Constellation Q2 2025 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-second-quarter-2025-results/); [DOE - Crane loan close](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-closes-loan-restart-nuclear-power-plant-pennsylvania)

chapters.title: From the 2012 Exelon merger through the 2022 spin to the AI inflection
chapters.body:
## Two Companies Before the Merger

Long before the corporate separation that created today's Constellation Energy Corporation, two distinct utilities occupied adjacent but strategically divergent positions in American power markets.

In Baltimore, Constellation Energy Group stood as the holding company for Baltimore Gas and Electric, a century-old regulated utility serving Maryland's central corridor, alongside one of the country's most aggressive competitive merchant-generation and retail-energy supply businesses. Under Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Mayo A. Shattuck III, a former Alex. Brown investment banker, the Baltimore company had built a national footprint in wholesale power, structured energy products, and retail supply far beyond what a BGE parent alone would have justified.

In Chicago, Exelon Corporation had assembled the country's largest nuclear fleet through its own 2000 merger of PECO Energy and Unicom Corporation, the ComEd parent. Under Chief Executive John Rowe, Exelon systematically expanded its reactor portfolio while managing the political complexity that came with operating in Illinois, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and the broader Mid-Atlantic.

## The 2012 Merger: Exelon Acquires Constellation Energy Group

The rationale that Rowe and Shattuck assembled publicly in 2011 and early 2012 was straightforward: an Exelon-Constellation combination would create the largest utility company in the United States by customer count, combine the nuclear fleets under a single operator, and integrate Constellation's competitive supply capabilities into Exelon's broader structure.

The merger was not frictionless. Maryland regulators extracted customer-rate protections before approving the transaction. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission also required structural commitments before clearing the deal.

The merger closed in March 2012. Exelon acquired Constellation Energy Group in a stock-for-stock transaction. Shattuck did not remain as a senior executive in the combined company. Rowe retired shortly after the merger closed, handing the CEO role to Christopher Crane, the nuclear-operations veteran who had run Exelon Nuclear.

## A Difficult Decade: Merchant Nuclear Under Pressure

What followed over the next decade was a sustained compression of the merchant nuclear model. From 2012 through the late 2010s, the expansion of natural-gas-fired generation, enabled by the shale revolution, depressed wholesale power prices in PJM and MISO, squeezing the economics of baseload nuclear plants whose operating costs were largely fixed. Several of Exelon's older, smaller single-unit reactors operated below cash breakeven through multiple years of the 2015-2019 trough.

Exelon's response was twofold: aggressive engagement with state legislators and regulators in Illinois and New York to secure zero-emissions credits for plants that might otherwise close, and a growing internal debate about the optimal corporate structure. The Illinois Future Energy Jobs Act of 2016 and the New York Clean Energy Standard kept several plants operating that might otherwise have been retired. But the regulatory patchwork was state-specific and partial.

## February 2022: The Separation

By the early 2020s, Exelon management had concluded that the regulated utility business and the merchant-generation business had fundamentally divergent profiles: different capital structures, different investor bases, and different regulatory regimes. A single holding company serving both constituencies was suboptimal for each.

The separation plan envisioned spinning off Constellation Energy Corporation as a standalone publicly traded company. Exelon would retain the six regulated utility businesses: ComEd, PECO, BGE, ACE, Pepco, and Delmarva Power. The nuclear fleet and the Constellation competitive supply business would transfer to the new entity.

The spin-off economics at inception were not especially flattering to Constellation. The company entered the public markets as a merchant nuclear operator at a moment when nuclear generation was not yet broadly valued as a scarce strategic resource. The equity was priced accordingly.

## The IRA and the Nuclear Re-Rating

The August 2022 passage of the Inflation Reduction Act changed that calculus structurally. The significance of Section 45U was not merely incremental revenue; it materially reduced the downside scenario that had made merchant nuclear economics so painful in the 2015-2019 trough. At low wholesale power prices, the credit could offset revenue shortfall and create an effective floor under plant economics.

## Three Mile Island and the Hyperscaler Template

The September 2024 Microsoft agreement crystallised what the equity had been pricing in the abstract. Three Mile Island Unit 1 had shut in September 2019 for economic reasons. What changed over the following five years was not a publicly disclosed contract price but the commercial willingness of a hyperscaler to sign a 20-year agreement that supported restarting a retired nuclear unit. That was enough to demonstrate that data-centre customers would commit long term to firm clean baseload power if the asset and grid location fit their needs. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Calpine and the Platform Extension

The January 2025 Calpine announcement, followed by the January 7, 2026 close, extended the platform beyond a nuclear pure-play into a broader merchant generation company. Calpine brought roughly 26.7 gigawatts of gas and geothermal capacity, meaningful ERCOT and CAISO exposure, and a deeper customer interface for large-load contracting. The combined platform was now one of the largest merchant generation businesses in US history, but it was also more operationally complex than the pre-deal Constellation. [Constellation - Calpine announcement](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-acquire-calpine-creates-americas-leading-producer); [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

---

Constellation entered the post-spin era as a merchant nuclear company at a trough valuation. By the frozen snapshot date, it had been re-rated as the principal scaled public vehicle for US nuclear and AI-electricity demand. The arc from Mayo Shattuck's merchant Baltimore company through the Exelon decade to Joe Dominguez's post-spin Constellation had taken fourteen years to complete, and it had culminated at a moment when nuclear generation's structural scarcity was again being monetised.

chapters.title: Nuclear fleet, gas-and-renewables generation, and competitive supply
chapters.body:
## A two-segment business

At the broadest level, Constellation operated in two principal legacy segments: Generation, encompassing nuclear, gas, hydro, wind, and solar production facilities, and Customer Channels, the competitive retail and wholesale supply business serving commercial, industrial, and residential customers in deregulated electricity markets. The Calpine acquisition added a third practical dimension, dispatchable gas-fired generation and geothermal capacity, that reshaped the company's dispatch stack even if management continued to report Constellation on its own segment structure. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

## The nuclear fleet

The Generation segment was anchored by the largest commercial nuclear fleet in the United States. In the 2025 Form 10-K, Constellation said it had ownership interests in 14 nuclear generating stations currently in service, consisting of 25 units and approximately 22 gigawatts of capacity. The fleet was concentrated in PJM and MISO but also extended into NYISO and ERCOT through the South Texas Project. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

Illinois remained the densest cluster by geography: Byron, Braidwood, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle, and Quad Cities. The PJM and Mid-Atlantic set included Calvert Cliffs, Limerick, and Peach Bottom, while the New York portfolio included Ginna, Nine Mile Point, and FitzPatrick. Constellation also held partial interests in Salem in New Jersey and South Texas Project in Texas. Customer Channels, rather than the operating nuclear fleet itself, was what extended Constellation's commercial reach into ISO-NE. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

Alongside the nuclear fleet, the Generation segment included gas-fired peakers, combined-cycle assets, hydroelectric capacity, wind, and utility-scale solar. These non-nuclear assets provided dispatch flexibility and hedging capability but remained secondary to the nuclear portfolio by a wide margin before Calpine closed.

## Licence renewals and the 80-year nuclear horizon

A structural feature distinguishing Constellation's fleet was the multi-decade licence runway secured through NRC-approved renewals. Nuclear plants were initially licensed for 40 years; the NRC's first renewal programme extended authorisations to 60 years, and subsequent licence-renewal applications pursued extensions to 80 years.

By the snapshot date, several units had already received or were pursuing second licence renewals. The 80-year authorisations materially altered long-term earnings visibility: a reactor licensed into the 2050s or 2060s was an asset of different economic character from one facing closure within a decade. The December 2025 renewals for Clinton and Dresden showed how directly licence life now intersected with AI-era demand and contracting narratives. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [Constellation - Clinton and Dresden renewals](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nrc-renews-operating-licenses-clinton-dresden-constellation)

## Section 45U mechanics in practice

At the merchant power-price levels prevailing through 2023-2025, most Constellation nuclear units were not simply living off subsidy. The credit's function was architectural rather than immediately cash-maximising. It supported the downside case. Constellation's disclosures described Section 45U as a hedge against soft power markets rather than a substitute for commercial contracting, and the interaction mattered because the company increasingly wanted to convert the fleet from a pure commodity book into a partly contracted infrastructure platform. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Customer Channels: competitive retail and wholesale supply

The Customer Channels segment operated Constellation's competitive retail electricity and gas supply business, serving commercial, industrial, and residential customers across deregulated markets. In 2025, the company said it served approximately 204 terawatt-hours of electric power load and roughly 800 billion cubic feet of gas. That made Customer Channels more than a sidecar. It was the commercial interface through which Constellation could see customer demand, originate structured power products, and package cleaner or firmer supply arrangements for large-load buyers. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

The segment also provided a natural hedge on a portion of nuclear output, reducing the proportion sold at spot market prices. The ability to originate and structure bilateral PPAs became the scaffolding on which the hyperscaler PPA pipeline was built.

## The Calpine platform extension

Calpine brought a different profile entirely. Constellation's announcement described Calpine as adding about 26,700 megawatts of gas-fired and geothermal generation across a fleet centred in Texas and California but extending through eastern power markets as well. The Geysers complex contributed about 725 megawatts of geothermal capacity, the largest geothermal operation in the United States. [Constellation - Calpine announcement](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-acquire-calpine-creates-americas-leading-producer); [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

The strategic importance was obvious. Nuclear delivered clean baseload. Calpine delivered flexible heat-rate and location optionality. Together, the businesses could offer large customers a broader menu: carbon-free baseload where nuclear was available, dispatchable gas where hourly reliability or regional location mattered more, and a much larger retail and structured-product reach.

| Segment | Capacity / scale | Primary markets | Core role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nuclear legacy CEG | ~22 GW across 14 in-service stations / 25 units | PJM, MISO, NYISO, ERCOT | Carbon-free baseload generation |
| Customer Channels | 204 TWh power served and ~800 Bcf gas served in 2025 | Deregulated US power and gas markets, including ISO-NE reach | Retail, wholesale, and structured offtake platform |
| Calpine (added platform) | ~26.7 GW gas plus ~0.7 GW geothermal | ERCOT, CAISO, and eastern organised markets | Dispatchable gas, geothermal, and data-centre adjacency |

## Hyperscaler PPA pipeline

The Microsoft contract established the commercial template, and the Meta contract at Clinton demonstrated that the template was not a one-off. By the frozen snapshot date, Constellation had publicly named Microsoft and Meta as the two nuclear counterparties that had signed long-duration baseload agreements. After Calpine closed, it also disclosed a separate CyrusOne data-centre arrangement in Texas through Calpine, underscoring that the customer-acquisition thesis had broadened beyond the nuclear fleet alone. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/); [Constellation - CyrusOne at Freestone](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-and-cyrusone-announce-agreement-support-new-data)

chapters.title: $23.6B revenue, $4.8B adjusted EBITDA, and the AI re-rating
chapters.body:
## The margin revolution: earnings quality changed faster than revenue

Constellation's financial story looked different once the official disclosures were laid side by side. Operating revenues were $24.442 billion in 2022, $24.918 billion in 2023, $23.568 billion in 2024, and $25.533 billion in 2025. That was not a straight-line top-line boom. What changed more sharply was the quality and visibility of earnings. Adjusted EBITDA moved from $2.667 billion in 2022 to $4.025 billion in 2023, while 2024 and 2025 company filings emphasised adjusted operating earnings per share of $8.67 and $9.39 respectively. The business had become less exposed to the pure merchant downside that defined the previous decade, even before long-term nuclear offtake contracts became more common. [Constellation FY2022 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2022-results); [Constellation FY2023 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2023-results); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## The 45U PTC: engineering a downside floor

The reason Section 45U mattered so much was scale. Constellation's 2025 Form 10-K said the fleet produced 183 terawatt-hours of zero-emissions nuclear output in 2025. At the statutory maximum rate of $15 per megawatt-hour, that level of output implied a gross theoretical credit value of roughly $2.7 billion before any phase-out effects or qualification assumptions. In practice, realised value was lower because the credit phases down as realised power prices rise and because the company increasingly layered commercial contracts over the fleet. But the existence of the credit changed the shape of the downside scenario. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

Prior to the IRA, merchant nuclear operated with no comparable federal backstop. Low gas prices could crush basin power prices, and the fixed-cost nature of nuclear operations left little room to absorb a sustained drop. Section 45U did not eliminate market exposure, but it materially reduced the probability that a broad power-price downturn would again push core plants into the economic danger zone.

## PJM capacity: the auction sequence that reset forward earnings

The second major earnings lever was capacity. PJM's July 2024 auction for the 2025-2026 delivery year cleared at $269.92 per megawatt-day, a step-change from the prior trough levels. PJM's next auction, for 2026-2027, cleared at $329.17 per megawatt-day. In December 2025, the 2027-2028 auction cleared at $333.44 per megawatt-day, and Constellation disclosed in a subsequent 8-K that it had cleared about 17,950 megawatts in that auction. The compounding effect of those results was straightforward: a meaningful fraction of the fleet's forward earnings stack had been repriced before any additional hyperscaler contract was signed. [PJM 2025-2026 BRA release](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2024-releases/20240730-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-sufficient-resources-to-meet-rto-reliability-requirement.pdf); [PJM 2026-2027 BRA page](https://www.pjm.com/markets-and-operations/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2026-2027-base-residual-auction); [PJM 2027-2028 BRA release](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2025-releases/20251217-pjm-auction-procures-134479-mw-of-generation-resources.pdf); [Constellation 8-K on 2027-2028 auction](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000186827525000112/ceg-20251217.htm)

## The PPA economics: what was and was not disclosed

Constellation's primary disclosures did not provide a Microsoft power price or a project-level payback schedule. What the company did disclose was more limited but still economically meaningful: Microsoft signed a 20-year agreement tied to the full 835-megawatt output of the restarted Crane unit; Meta signed a separate 20-year agreement for Clinton beginning in June 2027; and Constellation tied those agreements to continued plant operations, plant uprates, and the ability to convert previously merchant output into contracted cash flow. That was enough to support the commercial thesis without inventing an undisclosed tariff. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Calpine: financing the extension

Constellation's January 2025 announcement described the Calpine transaction as an equity purchase price of roughly $16.4 billion, consisting of 50 million CEG shares and $4.5 billion of cash, plus the assumption of about $12.7 billion of Calpine net debt. The company explicitly framed the deal around portfolio complementarity rather than a simple volume build. Calpine brought flexible gas generation, geothermal capacity, and a wider geographic and customer footprint. When the deal closed on January 7, 2026, Constellation said the combined platform had 55 gigawatts of capacity and roughly 2.5 million customer accounts. [Constellation - Calpine announcement](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-acquire-calpine-creates-americas-leading-producer); [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

## Capital allocation

Through the post-spin years, capital allocation ran through four channels: a common dividend, opportunistic share repurchases, nuclear sustaining and uprate investment, and finally the Crane restart and Calpine integration. The 2025 Form 10-K said that, since 2023, the board had authorised up to $3 billion of share repurchases and that about $593 million of authority remained as of December 31, 2025. The same filing said the board had approved a 10 percent increase in the 2026 quarterly dividend versus the 2025 rate. Those disclosures mattered because they showed that, even after a transformational acquisition, management still wanted the market to view the combined company as capable of both reinvestment and shareholder distributions. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Reading the earnings architecture correctly

The important point was therefore not that every year after the spin had shown a higher reported revenue line. It had not. The point was that the earnings architecture had been redrawn. Section 45U supported the floor. PJM auctions repriced capacity. Microsoft and Meta began to carve merchant output into contracted nuclear supply. Calpine added a different but complementary earnings engine. By the frozen snapshot date, Constellation's finances looked less like those of a conventional commodity merchant and more like those of a platform operator sitting between wholesale power scarcity and very large, very creditworthy electricity buyers.

chapters.title: From the 2022 post-spin baseline to the 2024 record and Calpine
chapters.body:
## Standing Alone: 2022 and the post-spin baseline

Dominguez used the first post-spin year to frame what Constellation was, and what it was not. It was not a regulated utility earning a commission-approved return on rate base. It was a merchant generator and competitive supplier whose economics still depended heavily on wholesale markets. Official 2022 results showed operating revenues of $24.442 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $2.667 billion, numbers that reflected the elevated power-price environment but still sat inside a pre-45U risk structure. [Constellation FY2022 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2022-results)

## The IRA and the first earnings re-rating

Through 2023, the commercial and finance teams were working through how the IRA changed the shape of the business. Revenue for 2023 rose to $24.918 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $4.025 billion. The jump mattered because it came before any disclosed Microsoft or Meta-style bilateral nuclear contract. Investors were already beginning to capitalise the idea that a fleet this large, now protected by Section 45U, no longer carried the same downside as the older merchant nuclear model. [Constellation FY2023 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2023-results); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

By late 2023 and into 2024, the AI and data-centre demand thesis was increasingly visible in management commentary. What had begun as a policy and commodity story was becoming a scarcity-and-contracting story.

## September 2024: the Microsoft transaction

The Microsoft agreement was transformative because it showed that a hyperscaler would sign a 20-year contract around a single restarted nuclear asset. The company did not disclose the strike price, but it did disclose the critical commercial architecture: full-facility scale, long tenor, investment-grade corporate counterparty, and a physical plant whose restart economics would not have been credible in 2019. That structure effectively turned Three Mile Island Unit 1 from a stranded retirement into a nationally watched test case for AI-era nuclear contracting. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## FY2024 results and the Calpine announcement

The next formal set of numbers confirmed that the re-rating was not purely narrative. Operating revenues for 2024 were $23.568 billion and adjusted operating earnings were $8.67 per share, according to the 2025 Form 10-K. By then, investors were also weighing the January 2025 Calpine announcement, which proposed a different sort of transformation: not just better monetisation of nuclear, but a far larger generation and customer platform spanning nuclear, gas, geothermal, and competitive supply. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [Constellation - Calpine announcement](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-acquire-calpine-creates-americas-leading-producer)

| Fiscal Year | Operating revenue (USD bn) | Adjusted EBITDA (USD bn) | Adjusted operating EPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 24.442 | 2.667 | - |
| 2023 | 24.918 | 4.025 | - |
| 2024 | 23.568 | - | 8.67 |
| 2025 | 25.533 | - | 9.39 |

The table also shows the shift in the company's own disclosure emphasis: 2022 and 2023 were framed around adjusted EBITDA, while 2024 and 2025 were more cleanly supported through operating revenue and adjusted operating earnings per share.

## 2025: the pipeline broadened

June 2025 mattered almost as much as September 2024. The Meta agreement at Clinton showed that the Microsoft template was exportable to a different plant, a different state policy backdrop, and a different hyperscale counterparty. Constellation said the agreement would begin in June 2027, support operation into mid-century, and fund a 30-megawatt uprate expected to be complete in 2029. The company's narrative was shifting from "one landmark deal" to "an emerging contracting framework." [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

That same year, PJM's capacity market continued to tighten and the company accelerated Crane's expected return-to-service schedule into 2027. In other words, the earnings story was being reinforced by both the bilateral contract path and the market-structure path. [Constellation Q2 2025 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-second-quarter-2025-results/); [PJM 2026-2027 BRA page](https://www.pjm.com/markets-and-operations/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2026-2027-base-residual-auction)

## Entering 2026: a different scale class

The Calpine transaction closed on January 7, 2026. By the time Constellation reported full-year 2025 results the next month, management was presenting a company with 55 gigawatts of capacity, about 2.5 million customer accounts, a newly expanded data-centre contracting lane through Calpine, and 2025 operating revenues of $25.533 billion with adjusted operating earnings of $9.39 per share. [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas); [Constellation FY2025 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

The earnings arc from the 2022 baseline through the frozen snapshot date therefore described a real change in category. Constellation had started life as a public merchant nuclear survivor. By May 2026, it had become the principal large-cap equity through which investors could express a view on US nuclear scarcity, PJM capacity tightness, and AI-data-centre electricity demand.

chapters.title: Dominguez, Shattuck, Eggers, and the nuclear-operator board
chapters.body:
## Dominguez at the helm: the CEO mandate

Joseph Dominguez inherited a peculiar mandate at the spin: build a coherent identity for a company that was simultaneously the largest US nuclear fleet operator, a competitive retail electricity supplier, and a merchant generation business whose earnings were structurally correlated to commodity power prices.

Dominguez was a natural fit. A mechanical engineer from the New Jersey Institute of Technology, he later took a law degree *magna cum laude* from Rutgers before serving as an assistant US attorney in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. His energy career was built at Exelon across regulatory and government affairs — he served as EVP for governmental and regulatory affairs before becoming chief executive of ComEd, Exelon's Illinois T&D subsidiary serving more than four million customers.

What the ComEd tenure gave Dominguez was precisely the stakeholder management and political engagement that merchant power generation requires. Nuclear relicensing, capacity market design advocacy at FERC, state zero-emission credit programmes, and ultimately the IRA Section 45U negotiation — all involved the same combination of regulatory command and political coalition-building that had defined his regulated-utility years. At the September 2024 Microsoft announcement, Dominguez articulated the commercial thesis:

> "The agreement marks the dawn of a new era of nuclear energy. It demonstrates nuclear's capability to meet the demands of our modern economy and confirms our belief that nuclear energy is essential to a clean energy future."

## The CFO function: Eggers, Smith, and the capital structure trajectory

Daniel Eggers's background was unusual among utility CFOs: approximately eighteen years at Credit Suisse, where he co-headed US energy equity research, before moving to Exelon's IR and corporate finance function. That analytical heritage made him an unusually adept communicator — in three consecutive years he won [Institutional Investor](https://www.institutionalinvestor.com)'s best CFO award for the utilities sector (2023, 2024, and 2025).

With the Calpine close, Eggers transitioned to Senior Executive Vice President for Finance and Data Economy — a title acknowledging both the expanded balance sheet and emerging AI data centre energy ambitions. Shane Smith, who had spent twenty years in the finance organisation and led treasury through the Calpine deal structuring, ascended to the CFO seat.

## The operational core

Bryan Hanson, as Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Generation Officer, carries the company's largest single operational responsibility: the safe and reliable operation of more than 170 generating units coast-to-coast. Hanson's career was spent almost entirely within nuclear operations — beginning at the plant level, extending through fleet-wide oversight at Exelon Nuclear, and reaching the executive position now encompassing the post-Calpine portfolio. He chaired the 2025 American Nuclear Society Annual Conference.

James McHugh, as Chief Commercial Officer, runs the organisation through which the hyperscaler PPA framework was developed. McHugh previously served as CEO of the Constellation subsidiary within Exelon Generation and held senior wholesale trading roles dating to the early Exelon Power Team years. His team manages wholesale hedging across PJM, MISO, NYISO, and ISO-NE and builds the pipeline of hyperscaler engagements.

Kathleen Barron, as Executive Vice President and Senior Advisor to the CEO, brought thirty years of energy policy and regulatory law. She served as Deputy General Counsel at FERC before joining Constellation's predecessor in 2010. Her fifteen years in government affairs made her the principal architect of the engagement that contributed to the IRA nuclear provisions. Barron announced plans to retire in 2026.

David Dardis, as Chief External Affairs and Growth Officer, combines legal leadership with new development. He served as legal adviser to FERC Chairman Joseph Kelliher during the Energy Policy Act of 2005 implementation before joining in 2007. His nearly two decades encompassed complex M&A execution including Calpine, major contract negotiations, and national energy policy advocacy.

## The board: expertise calibrated to a merchant nuclear business

The Constellation Energy board assembled at the February 2022 spin carried a disciplined composition logic: technical nuclear expertise, financial markets depth, large industrial operating experience, and regulatory familiarity — with none of the conventions that typically dominate a regulated transmission-and-distribution company's governance structure.

**Robert J. Lawless** served as non-executive Chairman, and his tenure with the Constellation enterprise was longer than virtually any other current board member. Lawless had first joined the Constellation Energy Group board in 2002 — a full decade before the original group merged into Exelon — and had continued on the Exelon board through the 2022 separation, arriving at the new CEG as Chairman at inception. His operating career was as Chairman, President, and CEO of McCormick & Company, the Fortune 500 spice and flavoring manufacturer: a background that brought large-enterprise operational governance discipline rather than sector-specific nuclear expertise, paired with twenty-plus years of direct institutional memory of the Constellation and Exelon nuclear-fleet businesses across multiple market cycles.

**Yves C. de Balmann** brought the deepest capital markets pedigree on the board. He served as Co-Head of Deutsche Bank's Global Investment Bank and as Co-Chairman and Co-CEO of BT Alex. Brown — the bulge-bracket investment banking operation within Bankers Trust — before building Bregal Investments, a private equity platform for the Brenninkmeijer family, from inception to more than €18 billion in assets under management. Critically, de Balmann also served on the original Constellation Energy Group board from 2003 to 2012, giving him direct prior exposure to the merchant nuclear business before it became part of Exelon. He chaired the Compensation Committee and sat on Corporate Governance. As the company navigated the Calpine financing structure, the hyperscaler PPA economics, and the evolving capital return programme, his transactional and capital markets depth was structurally relevant in ways that few other board members could replicate.

**Admiral John M. Richardson** provided the board's most direct nuclear technical oversight. Richardson served as the 31st Chief of Naval Operations — the highest-ranking officer in the US Navy — and before that as Director of Naval Reactors, the position responsible for the full life-cycle management and regulatory compliance of more than ninety reactors aboard nuclear-powered warships. The combination of engineering credentials (physics at the Naval Academy; electrical engineering at MIT and Woods Hole) with regulatory experience managing a naval nuclear fleet larger than any commercial operator made him uniquely qualified to chair the Nuclear Oversight Committee — the standing committee with direct responsibility over Constellation's fleet safety programme.

**Dhiaa Jamil** complemented Richardson's credentials with commercial utility nuclear operations experience. Jamil spent forty-one years at Duke Energy, rising to Chief Nuclear Officer overseeing the largest regulated nuclear fleet in the country before serving as Chief Operating Officer until his 2023 retirement. His direct management of the Duke-Progress Energy nuclear integration — twelve units across two organisations — provided a merger-integration reference that was relevant as Constellation absorbed the Calpine fleet. He served on both the Compensation and Nuclear Oversight committees.

**Bradley M. Halverson** chaired the Audit and Risk Committee. His operating background was as Group President and CFO of Caterpillar — a Fortune 100 capital-intensive industrial company with global treasury, financial reporting, and risk management complexity. His public accounting origins at Price Waterhouse, combined with his ongoing audit committee chairmanship at Sysco Corporation, provided technical financial governance depth.

**Charles L. Harrington** served as Corporate Governance Committee Chair with a career that combined engineering and technology leadership with large organisation management. As Chairman, CEO, and President of Parsons Corporation, he oversaw cybersecurity, national security contracting, and complex critical infrastructure programmes directly relevant to Constellation's nuclear regulatory environment and broader infrastructure positioning.

**Julie Holzrichter** brought risk management and large-scale systems experience from her decade as Chief Operating Officer of CME Group, the world's leading derivatives marketplace. Operational risk, regulatory compliance, technology platform management, and the integration of multiple multi-billion-dollar exchange acquisitions during her CME tenure mapped onto Constellation's trading, retail, and risk management businesses.

**Ashish Khandpur** joined the board from a career in advanced materials and industrial technology, including the Research and Development leadership and CTO role at 3M Corporation, and subsequently the CEO and Chairman position at Avient Corporation. His innovation and technology orientation was increasingly relevant as Constellation sought to articulate its positioning in the AI data centre energy ecosystem.

**Eileen Paterson** arrived in December 2024 with aerospace and defence operating credentials — she had been CEO of Aerojet Rocketdyne, a major defence propulsion company — and brought a US Army aviation background that added an operational dimension distinct from the finance and industrial profiles elsewhere on the board. She served on the Nuclear Oversight and Corporate Governance committees.

**Nneka Rimmer** brought strategy consulting depth — fifteen years at Boston Consulting Group, where she became the firm's first Black female partner — alongside operational experience as President of McCormick's Global Flavors and Extracts division and chief transformation officer of the same business. Her M&A advisory and execution track record, including the largest acquisition in McCormick history, was directly applicable to a board overseeing a $26.6 billion integration.

## Composition thesis

Read as an ensemble, the board's composition reflected neither the regulatory-compact heritage of a traditional investor-owned utility nor the financial-engineering orientation of a private equity-backed merchant generator. It was instead calibrated to the specific demands of a post-2022 nuclear pure-play: technical oversight of an operationally complex and heavily regulated nuclear fleet (Richardson, Jamil, Paterson); financial and transactional governance of a merchant business with large capital market exposure (de Balmann, Halverson, Holzrichter); industrial operating depth (Harrington, Khandpur, Rimmer); and a Chairman in Lawless whose two decades of Constellation-enterprise board experience provided institutional continuity across every structural iteration of the business since the Constellation Energy Group's independent years. The Nuclear Oversight Committee — a standing committee with no equivalent on most large-cap corporate boards — was itself a structural statement about where the business's operational risks resided. The post-Calpine board carried the same logic, extended to a generation fleet that now encompassed gas and geothermal assets alongside the nuclear core that remained the earnings foundation.

chapters.title: Microsoft, hyperscalers, C&I customers, and the nuclear fuel cycle
chapters.body:
## The Crane Clean Energy Center: from template to financed restart

The Microsoft agreement mattered because it attached a 20-year offtaker to a retired unit, but the project only became more concrete once Constellation began to publish the operational path back to service. In its August 2025 earnings materials, the company said Crane was ahead of schedule and now expected to return to service in 2027 rather than the original 2028 planning horizon. In November 2025, the Department of Energy closed a loan guarantee of up to $1.0 billion to partially finance the restart. Constellation's 2025 Form 10-K repeated that the site, once operational, would have approximately 835 megawatts of emissions-free capacity. [Constellation Q2 2025 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-second-quarter-2025-results/); [DOE - Crane loan close](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-closes-loan-restart-nuclear-power-plant-pennsylvania); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

The structure was unusually attractive to a data-centre customer because it solved several problems at once. It provided continuous zero-emissions supply, remained inside PJM where a large share of US data-centre development was occurring, and came with a physical asset whose output could be tied to a named facility rather than an abstract renewable attribute book. Constellation's public materials repeatedly framed that combination, reliability, carbon accountability, and grid relevance, as the core reason nuclear had moved into the centre of the AI-power conversation. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Meta and the publicly named counterparty set

The Crane contract proved to be a template rather than an isolated event. On June 3, 2025, Constellation and Meta announced a separate 20-year agreement for the output of the Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois. Constellation said the agreement would begin in June 2027, support relicensing and continued operations into mid-century, and fund a 30-megawatt uprate expected to be fully complete in 2029. The company also said the deal would preserve 1,100 local jobs, sustain approximately $13.5 million in annual local tax revenue, and include $1 million of charitable giving over five years. [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

By May 23, 2026, Constellation had publicly named Microsoft and Meta as its two nuclear offtake counterparties. After Calpine closed, it had also publicly disclosed a separate Texas data-centre arrangement with CyrusOne through Calpine: in February 2026, Calpine signed a new 380-megawatt agreement for a CyrusOne facility adjacent to Freestone Energy Center, plus an exclusive Phase 2 arrangement for another 380 megawatts, and Constellation said the total under contract for CyrusOne data centres in Texas exceeded 1,100 megawatts. That widened the company's AI-load exposure, but it did not amount to a third named nuclear PPA. [Constellation - CyrusOne at Freestone](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-and-cyrusone-announce-agreement-support-new-data); [Constellation FY2025 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results)

## PJM capacity: forward visibility before a bilateral contract is signed

PJM's auction sequence was the other half of the customer and revenue story. The 2025-2026 base residual auction cleared at $269.92 per megawatt-day. The 2026-2027 auction cleared at $329.17 per megawatt-day. PJM's December 2025 auction for 2027-2028 cleared at $333.44 per megawatt-day, and Constellation later disclosed that it had cleared approximately 17,950 megawatts in that auction. Those auction outcomes mattered because they monetised reliability and scarcity before any additional hyperscaler bilateral was executed. [PJM 2025-2026 BRA release](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2024-releases/20240730-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-sufficient-resources-to-meet-rto-reliability-requirement.pdf); [PJM 2026-2027 BRA page](https://www.pjm.com/markets-and-operations/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2026-2027-base-residual-auction); [PJM 2027-2028 BRA release](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2025-releases/20251217-pjm-auction-procures-134479-mw-of-generation-resources.pdf); [Constellation 8-K on 2027-2028 auction](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000186827525000112/ceg-20251217.htm)

## Commercial and industrial supply: the quieter base business

The competitive supply franchise remained a large business in its own right. Constellation's 2025 Form 10-K said it served approximately 204 terawatt-hours of electric power load and roughly 800 billion cubic feet of gas in 2025. Company materials also continued to describe Constellation as a leading supplier to three-fourths of the Fortune 100. That mattered strategically because the C&I book gave management a broad view of emerging load demand, counterparty needs, and structured-product preferences outside the handful of giant hyperscaler names that dominated the public narrative. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

The value proposition combined physical generation, trading capability, and contract structuring. In practice, the retail and wholesale channel was a commercial laboratory. It let Constellation observe which buyers wanted hourly carbon-free matching, which wanted fixed-volume power, which wanted co-location, and which cared most about reliability support or tax optics.

## The nuclear fuel cycle: concentration without a near-term break

Constellation's own 10-K provided the cleanest account of the Russian uranium issue. The company said its nuclear fuel was obtained predominantly through long-term contracts for uranium concentrates, conversion, enrichment, and fabrication, including contracts sourced from Russia; that it held inventory in various forms across the fuel cycle; and that it had diversified supplier relationships and entered into contracts to increase the size of nuclear fuel inventory. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

The same filing said the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act became effective in August 2024, banning imports of Russian-origin low-enriched uranium into the US absent a DOE waiver, and that Russia imposed temporary export restrictions in November 2024 that required export licences for individual shipments. The company did not, in the primary materials reviewed here, make the specific public claim that it had itself secured a DOE waiver. What it did say was that the conflict and sanctions environment could disrupt Russian fuel supply and that it was managing the transition with inventories, advance procurement, and broader supplier diversification. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [Congress - Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act](https://www.congress.gov/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/1042)

## Why the supply chain mattered to the AI story

Constellation's AI-era narrative depended on more than customer appetite. It also depended on the ability to keep very old but still highly productive nuclear assets reliably fuelled and licensed while restart and uprate projects advanced. That was why the federal government mattered at multiple levels by the frozen snapshot date: DOE had closed a loan guarantee for Crane, Congress had changed the economics of existing nuclear through Section 45U and Russian uranium policy, and the NRC remained the gatekeeper for restart and long-lived licence extensions. Constellation's customer story was therefore never purely commercial. It was commercial demand sitting on top of a dense regulatory and fuel-supply scaffold. [DOE - Crane loan close](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-closes-loan-restart-nuclear-power-plant-pennsylvania); [NRC - Crane Clean Energy Center](https://www.nrc.gov/info-finder/reactors/ccec.html); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

chapters.title: Where Constellation sits against Vistra, NRG, NextEra, and the IPP set
chapters.body:
## Scale without parallel

The Calpine close created something that had not previously existed in the American power sector: a single merchant generation company combining the country's largest nuclear fleet with one of the country's largest gas and geothermal fleets. Constellation said the combined platform had approximately 55 gigawatts of capacity and about 2.5 million customer accounts. [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas)

Understanding where the company sat required mapping the competitive field carefully. The key question was not whether peers existed. They did. The key question was whether any peer combined comparable nuclear scale, comparable contracting optionality, and comparable post-Calpine geographic breadth.

## The merchant IPP peer group

By the mid-2020s, the listed competitive generation set had consolidated around a handful of meaningful names.

| Company | Approximate company-reported capacity | Nuclear exposure | Competitive read-through |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constellation (post-Calpine) | ~55 GW | ~22 GW across 14 in-service stations / 25 units | Largest nuclear platform plus newly enlarged gas and geothermal fleet |
| Vistra | ~43.6 GW | ~6.4 GW | Closest public merchant comp, but much smaller nuclear book |
| NRG | ~12 GW owned generation | None of consequence | Large competitive retailer with generation, not a nuclear contracting comp |
| Talen | ~13.1 GW as of March 31, 2026 | ~2.2 GW at Susquehanna | Important data-centre precedent but far narrower asset base |
| NextEra | Large regulated and renewables platform; direct nuclear overlap materially smaller than CEG | Point Beach plus Seabrook interest | Important sector scale reference, but not a close merchant nuclear analogue |

The peer figures above were taken from Constellation's close release and the most recent SEC annual reports or proxy materials for Vistra, NRG, Talen, and NextEra within the frozen window. [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas); [Vistra SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1692819&owner=exclude&count=40); [NRG SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1013871&owner=exclude&count=40); [Talen SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1541316&owner=exclude&count=40); [NextEra SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=753308&owner=exclude&count=40)

## Vistra: the closest public comparable, but not the same thing

Vistra was the nearest public comp because it too combined merchant generation with retail exposure and had acquired a meaningful nuclear fleet through Energy Harbor. But even on the company's own filings, the nuclear book was far smaller than Constellation's. That meant less physical optionality for plant-specific hyperscaler contracts, fewer relicensing and uprate levers, and less direct leverage to PJM nuclear scarcity even if Vistra remained a serious merchant power competitor. [Vistra SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1692819&owner=exclude&count=40); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Talen: strategically important, but much narrower

Talen mattered out of proportion to its size because the Susquehanna data-centre deal established the co-location precedent that helped validate the sector's AI-power thesis. But Talen was still a one-station nuclear story in a way Constellation was not. Constellation could point to a 14-station operating fleet, a restarted Crane project, and a second publicly named hyperscaler deal at Clinton. Talen could point to an important precedent and a much smaller asset set. [Talen SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1541316&owner=exclude&count=40); [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/)

## NextEra and the regulated utility landscape

NextEra remained the largest US utility-scale clean-energy franchise by breadth, but its nuclear overlap with Constellation was materially smaller and sat inside a very different business model. NextEra's relevance here was not that it could mirror Constellation's merchant nuclear contracting path. It was that large buyers could compare Constellation's firm, nuclear-led offer with a portfolio built more heavily around regulated utility service, renewables, and storage. [NextEra SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=753308&owner=exclude&count=40)

Duke, Southern, and Dominion were also important adjacent references, but they remained regulated utility businesses. Their nuclear assets sat in rate base, not in a merchant framework available for bilateral hyperscaler contracting in the way Constellation's fleet did.

## The structural moat

Constellation's moat rested on a fact that could not be recreated quickly: 14 in-service nuclear stations, 25 operating units, decades of NRC licence life, and an operating workforce built over generations. New nuclear construction in competitive markets remained too slow and too capital intensive to threaten that position on any near-term horizon. Existing plants, relicensing, uprates, and restarts were the practical path to new supply.

Section 45U strengthened that moat by supporting the downside economics of the existing fleet. PJM's auction outcomes strengthened it by increasing the value of reliable capacity. Microsoft and Meta strengthened it by showing that firm nuclear offtake could be sold directly into the AI-data-centre buildout. [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf); [PJM 2025-2026 BRA release](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2024-releases/20240730-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-sufficient-resources-to-meet-rto-reliability-requirement.pdf); [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/)

## The post-Calpine strategic position

Calpine resolved the main structural criticism of the pre-deal Constellation story: a nuclear pure-play could offer clean baseload, but it could not offer a full national menu of location, flexibility, and gas-backed dispatchability. After January 2026, Constellation could credibly offer nuclear baseload, gas flexibility, geothermal output, competitive retail and wholesale supply, and a much larger set of potential interconnection or co-location solutions. That was why the company began to look less like a narrow nuclear equity and more like a broad power-solutions platform with a nuclear core. [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas); [Constellation - CyrusOne at Freestone](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-and-cyrusone-announce-agreement-support-new-data)

The remaining question was whether that scale would produce durable excess returns or merely a larger, more complicated merchant generator. By the frozen snapshot date, the evidence still favoured the former interpretation, but only if management could keep turning unique physical assets into long-duration contracts faster than competitors could imitate the commercial model.

chapters.title: From the 2022 spin through TMI to the Calpine close
chapters.body:
## Event timeline summary

The equity opened to cautious reception at the February 2022 spin. Merchant nuclear operators carried an institutional stigma earned across a decade of plant-pressure episodes and policy fights. The critical policy variable, whether Washington would materially support existing nuclear economics, remained unresolved.

That question was answered six months later with the IRA. The official financial sequence then showed how quickly the earnings base changed: 2022 operating revenues were $24.442 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $2.667 billion; 2023 operating revenues were $24.918 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $4.025 billion; 2024 operating revenues were $23.568 billion with adjusted operating earnings of $8.67 per share; and 2025 operating revenues were $25.533 billion with adjusted operating earnings of $9.39 per share. The progression mattered because it showed a company whose earnings quality was strengthening even when the revenue line did not move in a straight line. [Constellation FY2022 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2022-results); [Constellation FY2023 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2023-results); [Constellation 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868275/000155278126000142/e26100_ceg-ars.pdf)

## Three Mile Island: from closure to template

The backstory remained a shutdown decision made before Constellation existed in its current form. In September 2019, Exelon had shut Three Mile Island Unit 1 for economic reasons. What changed by September 2024 was the combination of Section 45U, AI-led load growth, and a Microsoft contract willing to underwrite a 20-year restart case. By August 2025, the company had accelerated the expected return to service into 2027, and by November 2025 DOE had closed up to $1.0 billion of financing support. [Constellation - Crane launch](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-launch-crane-clean-energy-center-restoring-jobs); [Constellation Q2 2025 results](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-reports-second-quarter-2025-results/); [DOE - Crane loan close](https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-closes-loan-restart-nuclear-power-plant-pennsylvania)

## Forward catalysts

From the frozen snapshot date, the principal near-term catalysts fell into four clusters. First was Calpine integration, because the platform had only been combined for a few months. Second was Crane, where NRC timing and restart execution still sat on the critical path for Microsoft-linked revenue. Third was the broader data-centre contracting lane, where the company had already publicly named Microsoft, Meta, and CyrusOne in different parts of the platform. Fourth was licence duration: NRC approvals at Clinton and Dresden had already reinforced the long-life thesis, and future relicensing decisions would continue to extend the cash-flow runway of the fleet. [Constellation - Calpine close](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-completes-calpine-transaction-powering-americas); [Constellation - Meta and Clinton](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear/); [Constellation - CyrusOne at Freestone](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-and-cyrusone-announce-agreement-support-new-data); [Constellation - Clinton and Dresden renewals](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nrc-renews-operating-licenses-clinton-dresden-constellation)
